paper.title: The SM3 Cryptographic Hash Function (GB/T 32905-2016)
authors: Y. Yang (authors of the CFRG draft); algorithm published by the State Cryptography Administration of China

program.how: written for ounce-core from Sections 4 and 5 of the draft (IV, T_j, FF/GG, P0/P1, message expansion, compression, padding); no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: SM3 of "abc" (1 block) and of "abcd" repeated 16 times (2 blocks) gives the draft's two published 256-bit digests

for each of the three compressed blocks: the 68 expanded words W, the 64 words W', and the 8 registers after each of the 64 rounds equal the draft's Appendix A tables, and the chaining value V_1 of example 2 matches (591 published values in all)

expected_values_source.what: the worked examples of Appendix A of the draft (examples 1 and 2 of GB/T 32905-2016): expanded message words, per-round register values, chaining value and digests
expected_values_source.note: the values are data, copied as numbers (extracted from the draft text by a script); the draft's sample C implementation was not copied. The source is an expired Internet-Draft, not the Chinese standard itself, which was not fetched

negative_control: built with -DSM3_T2=0x7a879d8bU (one bit of the round constant T_j for rounds 16..63 changed), 428 of 591 values match (the 16 early rounds still agree), and the program exits 1
not_checked: security claims and the draft's design rationale or cryptanalysis sections
messages other than the two worked examples (no long-message or multi-length vectors)
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 591 published SM3 intermediate values and digests of the draft's two examples. It does not show the security claims hold.
